"The Sprinto API Playground is a browser-based GraphQL explorer that lets you interact with the Sprinto Developer API without installing any client libraries or GraphQL tools... You can use the playground to explore the API schema, test queries and mutations, and validate responses in real time." The explorer is hosted on the live regional apps (e.g. https://eu.sprinto.com/dev-api/explorer) and requires a Sprinto account with administrator privileges and a valid API key; requests run against the live tenant. The explorer endpoints answer a CloudFront 403 to non-browser clients, so runnability is grounded in the vendor docs text.

"The Sprinto Developer API is built using GraphQL and supports **introspection**. Introspection allows the API to describe its schema, including available queries, mutations, and response types." Schema description is key-gated introspection rather than a downloadable artifact: no OpenAPI or Postman download exists in the docs corpus, and the models page embeds OpenAPI fragments inside the docs page for the custom-integration sync API only.

A startup used Sprinto for compliance automation for about a year. At renewal they hit a technical payment issue and told their customer success manager, who acknowledged it. Even so, someone on Sprinto's finance team disabled their account because the due date had passed.

After their account was disabled, the customer said Sprinto took almost 24 hours to respond to pleas to re-enable it and up to 48 hours to resolve it. Because they operate in a regulated space, they called the outage a nightmare.

The customer tried to terminate for breach of trust after the lockout. Sprinto replied that its terms of service don't allow termination for convenience, required payment for the full year's contract (about $4,000) whether used or not, and threatened legal action if not paid within 7 days. The user felt Sprinto was not acting in good faith and was 'bullying' them.

The customer worried that regular Sprinto employees seem to have extended access to customer data, since a finance team member could disable their account. They said this made them uncomfortable continuing to operate with the platform.
